title: Nature as the basis of the economy
context: Evaluate the following statements to embed the economy in nature:
statements: Nature's services are essential for the production of goods and services.
Only tourism depends on nature; laptop production and insurances do without natural basis.
The services of nature are also the basis of our economic system.
Economic activities are carried out as an autonomous process, independent of social decisions about resource use.
Food and laptops are examples of goods whose production depends on natural performance.
tactical_explanations:
Bread on the plate and laptop on the desk look like pure market products, but it does not arise in the airless space. The section sets the services of nature to the beginning: they are indispensable for the production of goods and services. Food and laptops stand for the goods side, tourism and insurance for the services side.

Fields, materials, environmental services and landscape foundations are thus part of the same requirement, not an ecological niche next to the actual economy. Anyone who makes nature the backdrop, undermines this indispensability.

The statement is true.

To declare tourism as a natural dependency alone, the sample pairs of the text are broken down. Food and laptops are examples of goods, tourism and insurance service examples; all four are under the same indispensability of natural services.

Laptops are a good example, insurances as a service example; both need services of nature according to the section. The restriction to the holiday sector is therefore too narrow. To lead laptop production and insurances as nature-free contradicts the explicitly mentioned examples.

The statement is false.

Figure 13 does not aim at a single sector, but at the economic system as a whole. Nature therefore not only provides raw materials for individual products, but also the basis on which this system is running. The message remains simplified: without a biophysical sphere, no economy in this representation.

The statement is true.

Autonomy sounds like a closed cycle of prices and quantities. The final sentence of the section says the opposite: Economy is not an autonomous process, but an expression of social decisions about resource use, distribution and justice.

Those who exclude the use of resources separate exactly the level of decision-making that makes the presentation as the content of the economy. Society and the environment would then be outside the world, not embedded.

The statement is false.

Food and laptops deliberately double open the goods clamp: everyday food and technical hardware. Both productions are based on services of nature, not just agriculture. The couple prevents misacceptance, alone fields and forests hung on the earth system, while electronics would be free of nature.

The statement is true.

title: Who carries out economic activities
context: Evaluate the following statements on who is carrying out economic activities:
statements: Economic activities are carried out exclusively by privately run companies.
Households and communities carry out economic activities.
The public sector includes the state and NGOs in this presentation.
Only the government produces goods and services; private enterprises do not play a role in this.
Private-sector enterprises, the public sector, households and communities carry out economic activities.
tactical_explanations:
Only private companies are mentioned, two of the three companies fall under the table. Private enterprises, the public sector, as well as households and communities are distinguished as those who carry out economic activities. Government and NGOs are part of the public sector, households are not only on the edge of consumption.

The narrowing to privately run companies contradicts this three-way division.

The statement is false.

Households are not merely on the brink of the graphic as buyers. Together with communities, they are among the actors who carry out economic activities. So, supplying, working, asking and community economy are within the economy, not in an upstream privacy outside the system.

The statement is true.

The public sector includes state and NGOs in this presentation. Later, NGOs also appear in civil society; this does not change the first assignment to the simplified illustration. Whoever strikes one of the two lists and the other leaves the picture over.

For this statement, the explicit parentheses state and NGOs suffice.

The statement is true.

Companies are among the promoters of economic activities, in addition to households and the public sector. The state alone does not produce all goods and services; this is the result of several stakeholder groups at the same time. A monopoly position of the state as the only producer does not correspond to this three-tier division.

The statement is false.

The guideline is a three-way division of the executives: privately run companies, public sector, households and communities. All three carry out activities, take input from nature and return outputs. The sentence gives this list completely and leaves none of the three carriers away.

A fourth, unnamed super-authority is not needed for this. If you only count factories, you will not be able to manage, receive inputs and output the public sector and households.

The statement is true.

title: Inputs from the Earth System and Outputs back
context: Evaluate the following statements on inputs and outputs between economy and earth system:
statements: The economy receives inputs such as natural resources and environmental services from the Earth system.
The pollination of food plants is an example of an output of the economy into nature.
Climate gases and waste are examples of outputs returned to the Earth system.
The biophysical sphere in this representation denotes the earth system into which outputs flow back.
Economic activities take input from nature without ever returning waste or emissions.
tactical_explanations:
Metabolism begins in nature, not in the factory hall. Natural resources and environmental services come as inputs from the earth system into the economy. Pollination of food plants stands as an example of such a service, raw materials as material extraction.

Without this influx, the goods and services described would not be in the known form. The arrow direction here is extraction, not yet return of waste.

The statement is true.

Reading pollination as an output turns the arrow around. Pollination of food plants is an environmental service, i.e. an input from the Earth system into the economy. Outputs in the other direction are climate gases and waste that go back to the Earth system.

Those who declare the bee to be the emission of the economy confuse the two rivers, which just separate Figure 13: Retrieving natural performance and returning residuals and greenhouse gases.

The chart separates natural resources and environmental services from waste, emissions and other damage on the input side; pollination is clearly part of the input side.

The statement is false.

What the economy does not bind or store returns as output. Climate gases and wastes refer to the representation as examples that are returned to the Earth system, the biophysical sphere. Emission and residual material belong to the same return flow, not to the inputs.

The chart complements waste, emissions and other environmental damage as visible counterparts to resources and environmental services.

The statement is true.

The Earth system and the biophysical sphere are in the proposition as the same target of the outputs. The graphic frames the economy through this sphere, not through an empty space. Whoever exchanges the biophysical sphere with the social environment confuses the two outer shells: environment against institutions, norms and politics.

The statement is true.

A pure extraction process without return is not provided in Figure 13. Waste, emissions and other environmental damage flow back into nature, and all economic activities have an impact on nature. The claim that inputs would come without any output, pushes the right side of the graph and the core set over returns to the biophysical sphere.

This is exactly the return that makes the embedding visible.

The statement is false.

title: Atmospheric greenhouse gases
context: Evaluate the following statements on greenhouse gases in the atmosphere:
statements: Water vapour, carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide and ozone are among the most important atmospheric greenhouse gases.
Dinitrogen monoxide is also called nitrous oxide.
Greenhouse gases allow the entire heat emitted from the earth's surface to enter space without hindrance.
These gases form a kind of insulating layer in the atmosphere that retains part of the heat emitted.
Only carbon dioxide is a greenhouse gas; methane and ozone are not included.
tactical_explanations:
Carbon dioxide alone would be an unacceptable shortening of the box list. Water vapour, carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide and ozone are the most important atmospheric greenhouse gases. The formulas CH4, N2O and O3 refer to the same substances, not additional secret gases.

If you cut one of these, you shorten the list with which the section introduces the greenhouse effect. The insulating layer is created by this mixture, not by a single molecule, which you could take out of the list and declare as a single gas.

The statement is true.

Laugh gas is the everyday name for nitrous oxide, in the box as N2O. The double name refers to the same gas in the greenhouse list, not an extra next to N2O. Anyone who thinks nitrous oxide is something other than nitrous oxide, splits an identification that explicitly sets the representation.

The statement is true.

Insulation layer means retention, not free passage. The gases hold back part of the heat emitted from the earth's surface. The claim that the entire heat goes freely into space, removes precisely this insulation effect. Without partial retention, the temperature increase described in the next sentence would not be in the described logic due to higher concentrations.

The sentence misses the mechanism of the box. Higher concentrations can only raise the global average temperature because previously a part of the heat remains in the atmosphere; unhindered heat emitted into space would take this next step of argumentation.

The statement is false.

Heat radiates from the surface, the gas layer holds a part of it. The insulating metaphor explains this partial retention without percentages that the section does not provide. Neither complete lock nor complete loss describe the book formulation. Exactly the retained part is the core of the statement.

The statement is true.

Methane and ozone are listed in the same list as carbon dioxide, with water vapour and nitrous oxide. Only CO2 as greenhouse gas is incompatible with this list. The narrowing would make four of the five gases mentioned invisible and reduce the insulation mechanism to a single substance, which the box does not just mention.

The statement is false.

title: Human activities and climate change
context: Evaluate the following statements zu Ursachen steigender Treibhausgaskonzentrationen:
statements: Only the burning of fossil fuels drives the concentrations; deforestation does not matter.
Agricultural intensification contributes to the increase in concentrations of these gases.
Increasing concentrations of these gases lower the global average temperature.
The rise in global average temperature accelerates climate change.
The deforestation of forests is one of the human activities that increases concentrations.
tactical_explanations:
Three human activities are placed in the box next to each other, not one. Burning fossil fuels, deforestation and agricultural intensification increase the concentrations of the gases mentioned. To remove deforestation from this series removes one of the three explicitly mentioned levers.

The limitation with only makes the sentence wrong, because the representation describes a majority of causes. Whoever narrows the causes on the chimney, makes grubbing and intensified fields appear as climate neutral, although the box leads them as equal drivers of concentrations.

The statement is false.

More intensive agriculture is a driver of its own, besides fossil combustion and deforestation. It is one of the human activities that raise greenhouse gas concentrations. The sentence hits this middle link of the enumeration without denying the others and inventing without yield figures that the section does not mention.

The statement is true.

The causal chain runs from higher concentrations to higher, not lower average temperature. The insulating layer holds more heat, the global average temperature rises, climate change accelerates. To maintain cooling, reverses the described effect and separates the gas concentration from the temperature that the box is connecting.

The statement is false.

Temperature rise and accelerated climate change follow the higher concentrations in the same sentence. More heat withheld raises the global average temperature; this increase accelerates climate change. The sentence represents the last link of the chain without introducing degrees or target paths that do not contain the representation.

Without this temperature increase, climate change would remain unconnected with human activities that raise gas concentrations.

The statement is true.

To clear forests is in the list of causes besides fossil combustion and intensification of agriculture. Deforestation is human activity, which increases the concentrations of greenhouse gases. Whoever leads grubbing up as a natural background without effect, undermines this link. The sentence remains the book cause and invents no hectare numbers.

The statement is true.

title: Dependence of selected sectors
context: Evaluate the following statements on the dependence of economic activities on nature:
statements: All economic activities have an impact on nature.
Only individual sectors have an impact on nature; the other activities are considered to be environmentally neutral.
Fisheries, agriculture, forestry and tourism are highly dependent on natural resources and intact ecosystems.
Some economic activities are also directly dependent on nature.
Long-term existence and productivity of these particularly dependent areas depend directly on the preservation and sustainable use of natural foundations.
tactical_explanations:
The line of action is without exception of the industry. All economic activities have an impact on nature, even if the strength and form of the effect may vary. Neutrality towards nature does not know this sentence. Even those who do not fish or wood, returns in the logic of Figure 13 outputs.

The All-Ansage is the first half of the thought before direct dependence follows individual areas.

The statement is true.

Environmental neutrality for the rest of the economy does not stand. All activities affect nature; in addition, some depend directly on it. The distinction concerns dependence, not the claim that whole sectors left no trace. Whoever claims neutrality for all but a few industries, cuts off the all-statement and twists the second half of the sentence.

The statement is false.

The four-page list indicates high dependency: fishing, agriculture, forestry and tourism. They need available natural resources and intact ecosystems to a particular extent. Other industries may be affected, but exactly these four are the ones that the section calls highly dependent.

Insurances appear earlier as a service example of natural indispensability, not in this dependency list. The rate remains with the four mentioned areas.

In the long term, fishing grounds, soils, forests and destinations will only remain productive if the same foundations are maintained and sustainably exploited, which will link the four-point list to the next sentence of the section.

The statement is true.

After the all-out statement about the effect follows the limitation to dependence: some activities are also directly dependent on nature. Both do not exclude. All have effect, direct dependence have especially the resource-related areas. The sentence repeats the second half without denying the first.

The statement is true.

Conservation and sustainable use are the condition of continuation, not a voluntary extra. Long-term existence and productivity of the particularly dependent areas depend directly on the natural foundations. Whoever destroys them undermines their own basis of catch, harvest, wood and tourist landscape.

The sentence binds existence and productivity to the same protection.

The statement is true.

title: Economy in the social environment
context: Evaluate the following statements to embed the economy in society:
statements: The economy is embedded in a social environment.
The state, business, civil society and social groups are shaping this environment.
Economic processes are never the result of social or political negotiation, but purely technical processes.
Changed consumption habits and social values do not affect the economy.
The processes in society and nature have an impact on the economy.
tactical_explanations:
The basic formula of the subchapter is embedded, not a decorative image. The economy is located in a social environment that shapes actors, and at the same time in the biophysical sphere. Prices and quantities do not float freely over state, norms and groups.

Without this environment, the framework in which companies, households and the public sector are active was lacking. The sentence hits the social shell of the picture. Figure 13 therefore draws society as a shell around economic activities, not as an optional decoration outside the system.

The statement is true.

Four designers call the text: state, company, civil society and social groups. None of these groups remains decorative. The environment arises in interaction, not by a single sovereign alone. Whoever cuts one of the four, exactly thins the actor landscape that spans the section.

The statement is true.

The conclusion of the negotiation is that the list of actors is not an exception. Economic processes are always the result of social and political negotiation processes. Purely technical processes without society would remove state, lobbying, civil society, purchasing decisions and protests from the declaration.

The quantor never tilts the sentence against this always-even formula.

The statement is false.

Social feedback is based on changes in consumption habits and social values. The presentation explicitly mentions these channels in addition to the costs of environmental destruction. Anyone who denies them only leaves natural costs valid and undermines social feedback.

Consumption and values are economic factors in this presentation, not private taste outside the system. Both belong to the social environment that has an impact on the economy.

The statement is false.

Two directions belong together. Environmental destruction generates costs for the economy, society shifts demand and values. Both have an impact on the economy, rather than ending as a one-way road from the economy to the environment. The sentence summarizes precisely this retroactivity of society and nature.

The statement is true.

title: Central role of the State
context: Evaluate the following statements on the role of the State:
statements: The state does not play a role in this section for the economy.
The state passes laws, enforces regulations and creates economic conditions.
Tax policy and environmental requirements are examples of such a framework.
Only companies are allowed to impose environmental requirements; the state remains a spectator.
The state has a central role in setting, among other things, legal and regulatory frameworks.
tactical_explanations:
The central role is to formulate the text, not a marginal note. The state adopts laws, enforces regulations and creates economic framework conditions, for example through tax policy or environmental requirements.

Taking it out of the economy is contrary to this allocation and would deny the framework in which the company will act and which it will try to influence at the same time. In this picture, companies remain actors within the framework that work on it through lobbying but do not issue it for the first time instead of the state.

The statement is false.

Three tasks of the state are in one breath: laws are passed, regulations are enforced, economic frameworks are created. This is more than symbolic supervision. The framework in which companies then act is created politically. Without this formula of three, only private discretion remains, which the section does not describe as an order alone.

The statement is true.

Tax policy and environmental requirements are examples of the framework conditions. They show that the state controls taxes and obligations, not only via criminal laws in the narrow sense. Both examples belong to the same instrument box. The sentence repeats them without inventing tax rates or concrete limits.

The statement is true.

Environmental requirements are state framework conditions, not private standards of companies. Companies can also regulate themselves and start CSR initiatives, but do not replace the state requirement.

Making the state a spectator and only acknowledging the imposition of environmental regulations by companies is a distortion of the competence which the section assigns to the state as a central role. Self-regulation remains an addition, not a substitute for the requirement.

The statement is false.

The central point here is that without this actor the legal and regulatory framework is missing. Decrees, enforcement and creation of conditions form the described role. The sentence summarizes them without additional claims about concrete paragraphs. Companies remain actors within this framework, not its sole authors.

The statement is true.

title: Companies between framework and influence
context: Evaluate the following statements on the actions of companies in the social environment:
statements: Companies operate within the state framework.
Companies cannot influence the framework conditions because lobbying is excluded.
Self-regulation and corporate social responsibility initiatives are ways through which companies actively shape the framework conditions.
Lobbying is considered a form of active influence of companies on the framework conditions.
Corporate Social Responsibility completely replaces all state laws.
tactical_explanations:
First, the framework, then the action in it. Companies operate within the conditions set by the state. This does not preclude later co-design, but it does specify the starting point: they are not in a legal space. Laws, regulations, tax policy and environmental requirements apply, while the same companies are actively trying to influence the framework.

The sequence is therefore not accidental: first state framework, then action in it, then active influence over lobbying, self-regulation and CSR.

The statement is true.

They actively influence the framework anyway. Lobbying, self-regulation and CSR initiatives are explicitly the ways of this influence. Excluding lobbying, the first link of this list of threes breaks and claims a fainting power that does not draw the presentation at the moment.

Acting within the framework and editing the framework is not a contradiction in this presentation.

The statement is false.

Self-regulation and corporate social responsibility come directly after lobbying. Both are forms in which companies not only accept the framework but also co-form it. The presentation treats it as a real practice alongside state regulation, not as a decorative footnote and not as a substitute for all laws.

The statement is true.

Lobbying is the active influence of companies on the framework conditions while acting within these frameworks. Both are co-existing: being bound and co-creating.

The statement is true.

CSR supplements state law, does not replace it in this section. The state continues to pass laws and environmental regulations; companies can additionally initiate responsibility and give themselves rules.

Full substitution of state law by corporate social responsibility is not and would eliminate the central role of the state, which is described immediately before.

The statement is false.

title: Civil society as a critical body
context: Evaluate the following statements on civil society:
statements: Civil society includes NGOs, associations, science and media in this presentation.
Civil society confirms economic action uncritically and does not address any maladministration.
Only the state formulates expectations for sustainable economic development; civil society remains silent.
Civil society is a critical body that questions economic action.
It formulates societal expectations for sustainable and ethical business.
tactical_explanations:
Four building blocks fill the term: NGOs, associations, science and media. Civil society is thus broader than a single protest group or an authority. The list is in the sentence, which introduces it as a critical instance. Anyone who only lets associations or only press apply shorten the book list.

NGOs can also appear in the simplified picture of the public sector, which does not change this four-tier civil society group.

The statement is true.

Critical instance means questioning, not nodding. Mistakes are addressed by civil society, expectations of sustainable and ethical economics are formulated. Uncritical confirmation and concealment of maladministration contradict this functional description word for word. The role is counterweight in negotiation, not jubilee chorus of companies.

The statement is false.

Expectations of sustainable and ethical business are formulated by civil society. The state sets frameworks, companies lobby and regulate, civil society raises social demands. Stupidness is the opposite of the described role.

To lead the state as a source of expectation only, NGOs, associations, science and media are cut off from negotiation, from which economic processes are co-existed. In this reading, economic processes remain negotiation between several instances, not a monologue of legislation without critical public opinion.

The statement is false.

Questioning is the guiding verb of the functional description. Economic action is not accepted as given, but examined. This is exactly what makes civil society in this section a critical authority alongside state and enterprise. Without this questioning, the instance that addresses maladministration was missing.

The statement is true.

The content of expectations is sustainable and ethical, not an empty phrase. Civil society brings these demands into the negotiation process, from which economic processes are co-existed. The sentence takes the second half of the functional description and remains in the words of the section without inventing quality seals or standards numbers.

The statement is true.

title: Consumers, employees and co-design
context: Evaluate the following statements on individual and collective actors:
statements: Only companies and the state shape economic structures; consumers remain without influence.
Purchase decisions can influence economic structures and standards.
Labour mobility and protests are described in the section as behaviours with which actors participate.
Employees have no influence on economic standards in this presentation.
Consumers, consumers, employees are among the actors involved in behaviour and decisions.
tactical_explanations:
Individual and collective actors are also at the same level as state, company and civil society. Consumers are involved in structures and norms through purchasing decisions, labour mobility or protests. Influx would be incompatible with this sentence.

Those who only consider companies and authorities as designers are cutting off everyday life and acquisition from the social embedding of the economy. Purchase, change of job and protest are economic actions with normative effect in this logic, not private matters outside of Figure 13.

The statement is false.

Purchase decisions are the first of the three examples of behaviour mentioned above. They are part of the co-imposition of economic structures and norms, not only for private need-settlement. Demand becomes socially effective here: what households choose or avoid, shifts the offer. The sentence remains with this mentioned way.

The statement is true.

Labour mobility and protests complement the purchase. Those who change jobs or publicly contradict them have the same logic influencing structures and norms. The section explicitly lists these paths, rather than explaining economics only through prices without behaviour. Both examples are part of the co-design by individual and collective actors.

The statement is true.

Employees are in one breath with consumers. Their behaviour, including mobility and protest, is part of shaping economic structures and norms. Influence zero would be to remove this stakeholder group from the embedding. The section gives them explicit voice about decisions in everyday life and the labour market.

Without it, the connection between the social environment and everyday decisions that the section is making was lacking.

The statement is false.

The dual role of consumption and work covers everyday life and acquisition. Both groups are among the individual and collective actors who influence economic structures and norms through behavior and decisions. The sentence remains within the book list and does not invent any other groups, such as parties or courts, which this paragraph does not mention.

The statement is true.

title: Direct and indirect costs of environmental destruction
context: Evaluate the following statements on economic costs of environmental destruction:
statements: Environmental degradation is a major cost to the economy.
Direct consequences are limited to image losses, not infrastructure or production.
Destroyed infrastructure due to extreme weather events, production failures and rising insurance claims are direct consequences.
Crop failures, increased health costs and productivity losses are presented as direct infrastructure damage, not as indirect effects.
The costs can be divided into direct and indirect damages.
tactical_explanations:
Reactive nature destruction is expensive, not only morally relevant. The section speaks of significant costs for the economy and divides them into direct and indirect damage. Extreme weather hits infrastructure, failures hit production, claims hit insurers; later crop, health and productivity come as indirect burdens.

Those who deny costs ignore this very bridge from the environment in economic sizes.

The statement is true.

Image and advertising are not included in this sub-chapter. Direct consequences are destroyed infrastructure due to extreme weather events, production failures and rising insurance claims.

Image losses as a single or typical direct consequence are an invention outside the text and would draw the concept of costs into a marketing topic that the section does not deal with. Direct damage is due to investments, output and risk transfer.

The statement is false.

Three direct examples are in a series: Infrastructure after extreme weather, standing production, higher insurance claims. They directly hit investments, output and risk transfer. The sentence represents the book list of direct consequences without mentioning damage sums that the presentation does not provide.

Indirect loads such as harvest or health belong in the next basket, not in this row of threes.

The statement is true.

Harvest failures, increased health costs and productivity losses are among the indirect effects, not the direct infrastructure damage. To exchange the allocation, mixes the two cost baskets that are just trying to separate the representation.

Indirectly, this is the consequence of yield, health and performance, not the concrete crack on the factory wall after extreme weather. The sentence makes the indirect list falsely direct infrastructure damage.

Direct damage is due to destroyed infrastructure, production losses and insurance claims; the crop-health productivity series belongs in the indirect basket.

The statement is false.

The division is the breakdown of the cost-distribution. First the distinction directly against indirect, then the examples, then the long-term tightening. Without this two-parting, only an unsorted damage cloud would remain. The sentence exactly meets the sorting of the considerable costs set by the text.

The statement is true.

title: Long-term challenges and adaptation
context: Evaluate the following statements on long-term climate impacts and adaptation:
statements: The degradation of ecosystems and climate-related migration are exacerbating economic challenges in the long term.
Increasing investment risks and disruptions of global supply chains are among these long-term tightenings.
Adaptation to climate impacts does not require any investment after the section, because ecosystems regenerate completely on their own.
The presentation describes resilient infrastructures, renewable energies and sustainable economic models as areas of investment for adaptation.
Society has an effect on the economy exclusively through tax laws, never through consumption habits.
tactical_explanations:
In the long term, the burden list becomes harder than immediate storm damage. Degrading ecosystems and climate-related migration are not only investment risks and supply chain disruptions but also a tightening of economic challenges. These are economic burdens over time, not just moral marginal notes.

The sentence mentions two of the explicit intensifications, without inventing migration or hectares.

The statement is true.

Investment risk and global supply chain close the long-term list. Disruptions not only affect local crop, but connected production. Increasing investment risks increase or postpone projects, supply chain breaks interrupt inputs.

The rate remains at the aggravation level and does not supplement any key figures that the section does not contain.

The statement is true.

Adaptation requires significant investments, specifically in resilient infrastructures, renewable energies and sustainable economic models to ensure economic stability. Complete self-healing of ecosystems without the use of resources is not available.

The sentence negates the investment needs that the section stresses and claims that automatic regeneration makes the sale of the adjustment unnecessary. Economic stability is to be secured by precisely these investments, not by waiting until damaged systems recover completely by themselves.

The statement is false.

Three investment fields ensure economic stability in this logic: resilient infrastructures, renewable energies, sustainable economic models. They are the answer to climate impacts, not a substitute for the diagnosis of damage. The sentence meets the Bay of Grain and does not invent funding rates or annual targets that do not mention the representation.

The statement is true.

Consumption habits and social values are the social back channel to the economy. Tax policy is part of the state framework, but does not replace this social effect. Only tax laws and never consumption contradict the sentence about changed habits.

Two channels exist side by side: politics of the state and behaviour of society.

The statement is false.

title: Ecosystems as a protection against disasters
context: Evaluate the following statements on healthy ecosystems and natural hazards:
statements: Healthy ecosystems do not serve as a protection against natural disasters; only technical structures do.
Forests can prevent or mitigate flooding by storing and re-distributing rainwater in a controlled manner.
In high alpine regions, forests can intercept avalanches as natural barriers and protect settlements, traffic routes and infrastructures.
Wetlands are increasing floods because they cannot absorb and hold back water.
These ecological functions reduce direct damage to infrastructure and property and promote regeneration after disasters.
tactical_explanations:
Natural protection is the heading of this block, not a metaphor without consequence. Healthy ecosystems serve as protection against natural disasters; forests, alpine barriers and wetlands are the examples. Technical buildings do not exclude the representation, but he does not claim to protect concrete.

If you remove ecosystems from the protection, you can store rainwater, avalanche barriers and the sponge effect of the wetlands.

The statement is false.

The flood mechanism of the forest is to store and return again in a controlled manner. This can prevent or mitigate flooding. The sentence follows this hydrological picture without inventing the drain percentage that the section does not provide. The performance is in the temporal extension of the water, not in a total disappearance of precipitation.

The statement is true.

High Alpine adds the avalanche to the water reservoir. Forests act as natural barriers, capture avalanches and protect settlements, traffic routes and infrastructures from damage. The geographical addition of high Alpine regions is not imported from other chapters. The sentence represents the protection object and mechanism in the book order.

The statement is true.

Sponge, not amplifiers: Wetlands absorb floods and hold them back. Reinforcement would be the reversal of this buffer function. Comparison with the sponge makes the direction clear. Anyone who leads wetlands as flood drivers contradicts the recorded absorption and retention performance, which is supposed to reduce direct damage to infrastructure and property.

The statement is false.

Less direct damage to infrastructure and property plus better regeneration afterwards, that is the economic yield of ecological functions. Protection thus reduces exactly the direct costs that the previous sales describes in extreme weather and facilitates reconstruction. The sentence combines both thoughts without introducing damage amounts.

Ecosystems here act as a precautionary measure, not as a substitute for any technical security, but clearly as a reduction in damage. Settlements, traffic routes and property benefit twice: less destruction in the event and faster recovery afterwards, supported by forest, alpine barrier and wetlands.

The statement is true.

title: Biodiversity, resilience and innovation
context: Evaluate the following statements on biodiversity and economic development:
statements: Biodiversity in an ecosystem increases its resilience.
Biodiversity makes ecosystems more rigid, so they recover more slowly after disturbances.
By protecting biodiversity, we contribute to the stability of natural systems, which strengthens the resilience of dependent communities.
Biodiversity is an important source of innovation in pharmacy, biotechnology and agriculture.
Many valuable compounds and genetic resources do not come from nature and do not play a role for new products.
tactical_explanations:
Biodiversity and resilience are parallel, not against each other. A diverse ecosystem can adapt to change and recover faster after disturbances. Higher biodiversity means more, no less resilience in this section. The sentence takes the first functional statement before communities and innovations follow.

The statement is true.

Faster recovery, not slower: Biodiversity allows adaptation and faster regeneration after disturbances. Rigidity and delayed recovery claim the opposite of the mechanism. The quantor tilts the sentence more slowly into the wrong, because precisely mobility and recovery speed describes as a gain of biodiversity.

A rigid system would be the counter-image, not the consequence of biodiversity. Therefore, protection of biodiversity is aimed at mobile, rela tive systems and at communities whose resilience is attached to these systems, not at frozen natural museums.

The statement is false.

Two levels are set: first, the stability of natural systems by protecting biodiversity, then the greater resilience of communities that depend on these ecosystems. The lever in between is protection, not just an inventory of species.

The sentence represents both stages in the book order and keeps the chain nature, stability, community.

The statement is true.

Pharmacy, biotechnology and agriculture are the three fields of innovation. Biodiversity is an important source of innovation: many valuable compounds and genetic resources come from nature and lead to new products and technologies that drive economic development.

The sentence specifies the fields without inventing active substances or patent numbers that the section does not contain.

The statement is true.

The phrase reverses its origin and benefits. Many valuable compounds and genetic resources come from nature and lead to new products and technologies. To claim that they did not come from nature and did not play a role for new products contradicts both halves.

These very resources are driving economic development in pharmaceuticals, biotechnology and agriculture.

The statement is false.

title: Economy as a social expression
context: Evaluate the following statements on the interaction between economy, society and nature:
statements: Economic activities source inputs from nature and return outputs such as waste and emissions to them.
Economic activities are embedded in social institutions, norms and political rules.
The economy is an autonomous process, independent of social decisions about resource use, distribution and justice.
A simplified presentation of the economic cycle does not require many details, but nevertheless makes central connections visible.
Only enterprises carry out economic activities; households and the government do not play a role in this.
tactical_explanations:
The cycle of materials between economy and nature runs in both directions: economic activities obtain inputs from nature, such as resources and environmental services, and return outputs such as waste and emissions to them. Anyone who only looks at the extraction, undermines the return side.

The statement is true.

The second embedding concerns society: social institutions, norms and political rules enclose economic activities. Thus, economy is not only a metabolism with nature, but also a set of rules of society. Both embeddings, the biophysical and the social, belong together.

The statement is true.

No autonomous process, but rather an expression of social decisions about resource use, distribution and justice: this is how the section concludes. Autonomy would make these decisions invisible and would detach the economy from society and the environment.

The sentence repeats exactly the opposite position that is rejected here, and cuts out distribution and justice that are at the core of the argument. Resource use, distribution and justice are in this final sentence the content of the economy, not external morality that could be decoupled without changing the system.

The statement is false.

Simplification and expressiveness are not excluded. A deliberately simplified presentation does not require many details and nevertheless illustrates the central connections between biophysical sphere, social environment and economic activities. Complexity is not called arbitrary here and not complete every institution.

The statement is true.

Households, businesses and the state jointly carry out economic activities. To name only businesses, two of the three institutions are scrapped and contradict the three-parting in households, community, private enterprise and public sector. Economy is the embedding of several actors, not the organization chart of a single business economy.

The statement is false.

title: Needs in the future
context: Evaluate the following statements on the importance of sustainability:
statements: Sustainability means that the common system of economy and environment is able to satisfy the needs of people in the future.
A sustainable system only covers the environment and leaves the economy and society out of the picture.
Economic action is considered sustainable if it takes place within the planet's biophysical boundaries without destroying the natural basis of life.
An economic system that does not take these principles into account only endangers the environment and never its own stability.
Sustainable economic structures are designed to meet the needs of all people while promoting social inclusion and social cohesion.
tactical_explanations:
Sustainability aims at the common system of economy and environment, not at an isolated concept of nature conservation. People's needs should remain fulfilled even later. This is precisely the future capability of the section.

Anyone who sees only today's paragraph misses the point: the system must still bear tomorrow. The economy and the environment are thought of here as a unit whose performance is maintained.

Without this temporal extension, sustainability remains a label for today's production. The section begins with the system's ability to meet needs later, and that is the benchmark.

The statement is true.

To name only the environment leaves away two of the three fields that explicitly bind the representation together. Economy, society and the environment form the system that can be considered sustainable. A pure environmental formula without economy and society is too narrow.

Social inclusion and economic action within planetary boundaries are part of the definition. Anyone who performs social and economic activities does not describe the textbook concept.

Decisive action is to make business and society successful within biophysical boundaries and to ensure social justice. This is not possible if two of the three fields fall out of the definition.

The statement is false.

Staying within the biophysical limits and not destroying the basis of life is the operative condition. Economics must not use up the physical base of the planet. This is the bridge from the meaning of the word to the rule of action.

Without this limit, any growth would be sustainable as soon as someone uses the term. The representation links sustainability to planetary boundaries, not to a label.

The statement is true.

Ignored principles not only affect forests or waters. The presentation also explicitly mentions the stability of the economic system and social welfare as endangered. The narrowing to environment alone is therefore incorrect.

Those who ignore subsequent costs undermine their own business base because climate, resources and social cohesion are responsible for production. The absolute "never holds their own stability" does not hold.

The statement is false.

The needs of all people and social cohesion are alongside the ecological border, not behind it. Sustainable structures should cover and include, not only emissions. Inclusion is part of the design task. Sustainability is threefold: biophysical border, needs coverage, social support. The statement is a reflection of this combination.

The statement is true.

title: Resources back to the cycle
context: Evaluate the following statements on the topic of resource collection and sustainable economic structures:
statements: The crucial factor is how resources are taken from, used and returned to cycles so that ecological stress limits are not exceeded.
Once a company gains profit, its actions are automatically sustainable, regardless of environmental impacts.
Long-term successful business includes companies and consumers taking into account the impact on others and the environment in their decisions.
Sustainable and resilient economies should promote people's well-being while preserving the health of ecosystems.
Ignoring interactions between nature and economy is the safest way to achieve resilient systems.
tactical_explanations:
The drawing, use and return decide whether load limits are maintained. The presentation highlights the cycle of materials, not only the first production. Whoever brings raw materials and never returns them, drives the exceedance forward.

The design of the rivers is therefore the lever: recycling and recycling are part of the sustainability definition, not as an optional annex. Ecological load limits are not set by the first step alone, but by the entire path to recycling. Whoever only promotes and never returns remains in the linear pattern.

The statement is true.

Profit alone does not prove sustainability. A positive result can arise precisely because subsequent costs are passed on to the environment or third parties. The presentation links sustainability to limits and impacts, not to the profit and loss account alone.

An operation can be profitable and at the same time destroy livelihoods. There is no automatic between profit and sustainability here. Short-term return can make the account even more beautiful, while society and ecosystem bear the remaining costs. Profit is a success mark of the company, not the proof of planetary compatibility.

The statement is false.

Chapter 1.3 links long-term success to responsible action: including impacts on others and the environment. Section 2.2 explicitly takes this up again. Both companies and households are required to do so.

Without this inclusion, economies remain short-term, even if it still works today. The statement is made in the sustainability chapter of 1.3.

The statement is true.

Well-being and intact ecosystems are the double goal at the beginning of the section. Resilience arises when both are thought together. Human development without ecosystem integrity would be incomplete, vice versa. The formulation is conscious and, not or. The statement reflects this And.

The statement is true.

Fading interactions weakens systems rather than strengthening them. The entry point calls recognizing this coupling as crucial for sustainable, resilient economy. Ignorance is the opposite of the required attitude.

If you think nature and economy separately, you overlook that destroyed ecosystems undermine the economic base. The safest way is understanding, not hiding. The first sentence of the chapter makes the recognition of interactions a prerequisite for resilient systems. Whoever ignores them builds on a basis that describes the representation as endangered.

The statement is false.

title: Take, Make, Waste in production
context: Evaluate the following statements on linear economics:
statements: In many areas, economic action still follows the linear principle of extracting raw materials, producing, consuming and subsequently dumping products.
The possibility of reuse, repair or reuse materials is often consciously exploited in linear systems and never neglected.
A linear resource flow leads to increasing environmental impact, increasing resource consumption and increasing pressure on planetary boundaries.
This economic way can destabilise central biophysical systems such as climate, biodiversity, land and water.
Linear economy has no impact on economic stability or human well-being, because only the environment would be affected.
tactical_explanations:
Bringing raw materials, making, using, throwing away: this is the linear pattern that names the representation with Take, Make, Waste. It describes the still prevailing river, not a historical relic. Extraction without sufficient return remains the normal case in many areas.

The statement shows exactly this process. Ecological consequential costs of resource reduction, emissions and waste often remain outside of this strand. That is why the linear principle is not only a flow pattern, but a cost shift.

The statement is true.

Circular use is often neglected in the linear model, not exhausted. Reuse, repair and recycling would be the alternative, but they often remain unused. The absolute "never neglected" reverses the finding.

Whoever claims that linear systems always maintain cycles is supposed to and is confused. The presentation describes the gap, not the completion. Take, make, waste leaves repair and recycling as an exception, not as a rule. The formulation never neglected would mean that the linear flow is already circulating, which the section denies.

The statement is false.

Growing load, more consumption, more pressure on planetary boundaries: these are the mentioned consequences of the linear flow. The chain is causally laid out. Border is not relieved by disposal, but loaded. Linearity is not only a technical layout, but a driver of ecological exceedance. The statement captures this triple sequence.

Increasing resource consumption and pressure to follow limits because material after use leaves the system. Disposing ends private use, not the ecological load.

The statement is true.

Climate, biodiversity, land and water call the representation biophysical systems, which are destabilized under linear pressure. This is not a metaphor, but the named chain of effects. Destabilization meets the physical basis of the economy. Anyone who only sees waste mountains underestimates the system effect. The statement remains close to the enumeration.

The statement is true.

The consequences do not remain at the environmental limit. Climate crisis, loss of biodiversity and overuse also endanger economic stability and human well-being. The claim of a pure environmental matter is too narrow. Human beings and the market are attached to the same systems. The separation "only environment" contradicts the section.

The statement is false.

title: External costs of a furniture factory
context: Evaluate the following statements on external costs and short-term profit maximisation:
statements: For individual actors, it is often worth maximising short-term profits and reducing production costs, while subsequent costs are passed on to other or future generations.
External costs do not arise from the company or the consumers themselves, but are borne by society or by ecological damage.
Those who outsource emissions and social exploitation have thus internalized all social costs into the product price.
Climate crisis, loss of biodiversity and overuse of natural resources threaten the environment, economic stability and human well-being.
The intensive extraction of natural resources without a view of ecological limits of stress is already described in the text as being overcome everywhere.
tactical_explanations:
Short-term profit and reduced production costs can be expected for the individual company because the invoice is incomplete. Environmental destruction and social exploitation migrates as external costs to the outside or into the future. The incentive arises precisely from this shift.

The furniture factory, which saves wastewater by polluting the river, shows the same mechanism: privately cheaper, socially more expensive. The presentation describes this as an even more frequent pattern.

The so-called external costs, such as environmental destruction or social exploitation, arise in production, but do not end up in the business accounts. Future generations inherit the damage that today supports the profit.

The statement is true.

External costs are not in the calculation of the cause. Society or ecosystem they bear, although production and consumption trigger them. That is the definition, not a special case. Consumers pay the market price, not automatically the full consequential damage. The gap between price and total cost is the core of the argument.

The statement is true.

Outsourced emissions are not currently internal. Externality means that the product price does not contain the consequential damages. Anyone who equates outsourcing with full internalization twists the term. Social exploitation in the chain is explicitly an example of external costs. It does not disappear because it is not on the account of the end seller.

Internalization would mean making consequential damages visible in prices and costs. Outsourcing is the opposite step: the load moves to third parties, while the price remains incomplete.

The statement is false.

Three sets of consequences call this presentation in one breath: climate, biodiversity, over-use. They meet the environment and at the same time the stability of the economy and well-being.

Sustainable economy must therefore act within ecological limits and ensure well-being, not sacrifice one of them. The statement remains in this connection. A sustainable economy must therefore act within ecological limits and ensure well-being. The three crisis areas are not decorative, they justify the demand for new models.

The statement is true.

Intensive extraction without sufficient consideration of the limits is the initial finding, not a overcome chapter. The presentation says "still before". Everywhere the opposite of diagnosis would be overcome. New models are required because the linear pattern persists. The statement claims a state that the section does not describe.

The statement is false.

title: Kreislauf statt Entsorgung
context: Evaluate the following statements on the circular economy:
statements: In the circular economy, waste is minimised and resources are kept in the economic cycle for as long as possible.
Products, materials and raw materials are reused, repaired or recycled.
The aim is to maintain the value of resources for as long as possible and thus reduce environmental impact and create economic benefits.
Circular economy means once using raw materials and then completely dispose of them without returning them to the cycle.
A sustainable economy must operate within ecological limits and at the same time ensure the well-being of all people.
tactical_explanations:
Minimize waste and keep materials in a circle for a long time: this is the short formula of the circular economy. Stopping time replaces the fast way to landfill. The economic cycle becomes a storage of resources, not a run-through. Minimizing does not mean that there is never a rest, but the direction is clear against linear disposal. The statement hits the core.

As long as material remains in a circle, the compulsion to new extraction decreases. Minimised waste is the visible side of the same strategy to throttling the throughput through the sinks.

The statement is true.

Re-use, repair, recycle are the three levers for products, materials and raw materials. They keep the value in the system. If one of these practices is missing completely, the flow is approaching linearity again. The representation lists them as related ways, not as rival schools. The statement gives the list.

If the repair is missing, equipment ends up as waste early on. If recycling is missing, materials are lost. The three practices support each other because they keep the same value in circulation.

The statement is true.

The same sentence of preserving value over time combines ecology and economy: less burden and economic benefits. Circular economy is not a mere model of renunciation. Both should arise, not just one. As long as the value remains in the material, the pressure to take off again decreases. That is the desired double profit.

The statement is true.

Once used and then disposed of is the linear pattern, not the circular economy. Return is just the difference. The statement swaps the two models. Without return there is no circle, only a distance with end point waste. The teaching text expressly separates these logics.

The statement is false.

Ecological boundaries and well-being of all people are the double mandate for which new models such as the circular economy are needed. Both together, not as a substitute for each other. The sentence stands immediately before the introduction of the circular economy. Regenerative resource flows and social justice belong in the same reform package. The statement holds this parenthesis.

This requires models with circular economy, regenerative resource streams and social justice. Borders and well-being are the two guardrails between which to rebuild.

The statement is true.

title: Repair bonus and Circular Design
context: Evaluate the following statements related concepts of the circular economy:
statements: Repair bonus, circular design, durable products and urban mining are related concepts to the circular economy.
Sharing models and durable designs are called ways to make economic growth less polluting.
Remanufacturing, the reprocessing of used parts, can save raw materials, reduce emissions and create new economic opportunities.
Circular design is intended to promote disposable products in the teaching text and is in contrast to the idea of durable products.
The repair bonus does not belong to the vicinity of circulatory considerations, but only to the linear disposal logic.
tactical_explanations:
Four names are related concepts next to the circular economy: repair bonus, circular design, durable products, urban mining. The representation does not define them individually, but clearly assigns them to this field. Relation means: extend the same direction, value and use.

Whoever absolves them as foreign marketing terms contradicts the assignment. The statement remains with the list. Durable products keep the same material in use for longer, urban mining searches for material in the stock instead of only in the deposit. The list shows practical forms, not foreign fashion words from another theory.

The statement is true.

Sharing and durable design are in Brundtland's connection as ways to a less stressful type of growth. Sharing benefits and keeping products replaces part of the new production. That's practical, not just rhetorical.

Both approaches are gentle on extraction and emissions by extending or dividing use. The statement remains with sharing models and long-lasting design. Reprocessing and sharing replace part of primary production. The report mentions such ways to reduce environmental pollution and create opportunities at the same time.

The statement is true.

Reprocessing of used parts saves raw material, reduces emissions and opens up economic opportunities. Remanufacturing is explicitly translated and justified in this way. Three effects, one process. Opportunities arise because processing itself is value creation, not just waiver. The statement reflects this triple effect.

Used parts are not scrap but used material. Raw materials saving and emission reduction are running parallel to the new value added in the preparation.

The statement is true.

Circular design stands alongside durable products, not against them. One-way promotion would be the linear opposite. The assertion of a contrast twists the kinship list. Design for circle and durability aims at longer use, not at faster disposal. The statement is therefore incorrect.

The statement is false.

The repair bonus is in the same line of kin as Circular Design and durable products. Repair keeps resources in circles, disposal throws them out. The assignment to linear logic is wrong. Bonus for repairing makes durability more economical. That is circular policy in the sense of the section.

The statement is false.

title: Poverty as a task of transformation
context: Evaluate the following statements on poverty and sustainable transformation:
statements: The transformation of the economy is also intended to address widespread poverty as one of the most pressing problems.
Sub-Saharan Africa has a disproportionate share of extreme poverty compared to its share of the world population, according to the text of the teaching.
In Austria, a different definition of poverty is considered as the world's extreme poverty line: poverty-risking is the one who is below a threshold for the one person household.
Poverty does not occur in Austria by definition, because poverty is only a topic outside Europe.
Progress in poverty reduction can be stalled by weak economic growth, pandemic consequences and increasing fragility.
tactical_explanations:
Widespread poverty is the urgent problem that should address transformation. Circulation and regenerative flows are not isolated from social situation. Remodeling the economy and addressing poverty belong together. Without this bracket sustainability would only be technology. The section explicitly opens to the social question.

The statement is true.

The figure is called sub-Saharan Africa in exactly this disproportion. Geographical concentration is the qualitative point, not a memorable decimal point.

The statement is that although only a small part of the world's population lives there, a large part of the extremely poor are living in this region. The relation is the teaching point, not an examination of the exact percentage.

The statement is true.

Austria measures the risk of poverty at household income below a threshold for single people, not at the global poverty line in dollars. The presentation juxtaposes both logics. Definitions are contextual. Thus, poverty in developed countries is not invisible, but cut differently.

The global limit of extreme poverty in dollars per day and the Austrian threshold for the one person household measure different cuts of the same social question. Whoever equates them, blurs the representation.

The statement is true.

The claim that poverty does not occur here by definition contradicts the section. Europe is not excluded. Other threshold does not mean absence. Whoever locates poverty only outside Europe ignores the national measurement.

The statement is false.

Weak growth, COVID-19 consequences and fragility cites the presentation as the reasons why progress is slowing down. In low-income countries, rates can even be above pre-crisis levels. Stagnation is thus explainable, not puzzling. Poverty reduction is not an automatic process of time. The statement reflects the mentioned brake factors.

In low-income countries, poverty rates can even be higher than before the crisis. Time alone does not heal the situation if growth remains weak and the situation remains fragile.

The statement is true.

title: Wachstum gegen planetare Grenzen
context: Evaluate the following statements on the dilemma of economic growth and environmental borders:
statements: Economic growth, understood as an increase in economic activity, is often seen as a central solution to reduce poverty.
The current level of global economic activity already exceeds several planetary boundaries.
There is no dilemma because growth reduces poverty and at the same time never touches ecological boundaries.
Poverty reduction measures can create new economic and social risks in the long term through their environmental impact, especially if they are based on resource-intensive growth.
Sustainable transformation requires approaches that enable economic development within biophysical boundaries and promote social justice without crossing ecological tipping points.
tactical_explanations:
Growth as an increase in economic activity is considered to be a lever against poverty for many. The presentation takes this view seriously before it problems it. Central solution is the attribution, not even the proof of non-dangerity. Social development is often linked to this increase. The statement reflects the initial opinion that the dilemma creates.

On the other hand, growth is considered necessary to reduce poverty and promote social development. This claim is precisely the one that hits already exceeded borders and creates the dilemma.

The statement is true.

Several planetary boundaries have already been crossed. So today's level of activity is not harmless below the line. Long-term need fulfilment is at risk. Diagnosis is about to be squared. Without this overrun, the dilemma described would not be in this sharpness.

The statement is true.

No dilemma to claim, the tension that the section calls a central challenge is not being overcome. Growth is to reduce poverty and burden limits at the same time. "Never is the absolute that refutes the representation. Both sentences are true in theory and at the same time incompatible in the naive model. That's why it needs another kind of growth.

Measures against poverty can later create new risks through environmental consequences. The Absolute never touches the second page, which describes the representation as already exceeded.

The statement is false.

Resource-intensive growth can alleviate poverty briefly and later build new risks because ecosystems are tilting. The presentation warns against this long-term trap. Ecological effects of poverty reduction are part of the bill. Whoever only counts today's income increase overlooks subsequent costs for the economy and society. The statement holds this bow.

Resource intensity is the lever that triggers the trap: more activity, more withdrawal, more pressure on tipping points. Poverty reduction therefore needs different paths than pure more of the same pattern.

The statement is true.

Developing within biophysical boundaries, promoting justice, avoiding tipping points: this is the formula for transformation. It does not solve the dilemma by denying one side. Development remains allowed, but limited. Social justice is not the residual post of ecology, but in the same sentence. The statement fully reflects the demand.

Tilt points mark irreversible damage to biophysical systems. The transformation is intended to enable development without tearing these thresholds, and justice is not treated as residual items.

The statement is true.

title: Our Common Future 1987
context: Evaluate the following statements on the Brundtland report:
statements: The Our Common Future report was published in 1987 by the World Commission for Environment and Development (WCED).
He is also called the Brundtland report because Gro Harlem Brundtland was the chairman of the Commission.
The report notes that the economic growth needed to combat poverty must not lead to future economic problems by its environmental impact.
Brundtland argued that sustainable development was impossible because growth and the environment could not be reconciled under any circumstances.
The report describes the extent of poverty and various threats to sustainability and calls for a new type of economic growth with a much lower environmental impact.
tactical_explanations:
1987, WCED, Our Common Future: these are the basic bibliographical data. The World Commission for Environment and Development is the issuing authority. The date is at the end of the twentieth century, as the section emphasizes. Without this assignment, "Brundtland" remains a name without a document. The statement correctly reflects origin and year.

Our Common Future is considered one of the most influential publications of the late twentieth century. Year, commission and title belong together, otherwise the surname Brundtland remains empty.

The statement is true.

Gro Harlem Brundtland, as chairman, explains the second name. The report and the person are so linked in the text of the teaching. Brundtland report is therefore not another text, but the same publication. Whoever considers the nickname to be a later EU document fails to assign it. The statement follows the theory literally in the matter.

The statement is true.

The circle is squared: poverty needs growth, growth must not ruin the future economically by environmental degradation. The report considers this to be possible, but only under a new type of growth. The condition is negatively formulated: must not lead to future problems.

This is the condition at the heart, not a ban on any activity. It is true that growth to combat poverty is allowed, but under the condition that the environment should not be burdened in such a way that the economy itself will later break. This is the squaring that the report considers possible.

The statement is true.

The opposite of the position is impossible. The report calls sustainable development necessary and feasible. Compatibility is sought, not denied. Whoever claims incompatibility as a Brundtland theme confuses the diagnosis of the threat with the conclusion. The conclusion is the new type of growth.

The presentation explicitly mentions the new type of growth as necessary and feasible. It would be impossible to find another school, not Brundtland. Sustainable development is the name of this feasibility.

The statement is false.

Poverty and sustainability threats are all together as an object. The answer is growth, which is far less burdening the environment and increasing the capacity of the common system to satisfy people. Both describe the presentation as content. The new way does not endanger sustainability, it should strengthen it. The statement bundles description and demand.

Instead of endangering sustainability, the common system of economy and environment should be better able to satisfy people. The same report describes poverty and criticises growth.

The statement is true.

title: Sustainable development in Brundtland
context: Evaluate the following statements defining sustainable development:
statements: Sustainable development is a form of economic growth that satisfies the needs and wishes of the present without jeopardising the ability of the economic and environmental system to meet these needs and wishes in the future.
What we need, according to the Brundtland report, is a new type of economic growth that is far less polluting the environment.
Sustainability in the text of the teaching means exclusively maximizing today's profits without considering future needs.
This new type of growth is intended to increase the capacity of the common system of economy and environment to satisfy people.
The Brundtland report completely ignores poverty and is limited to technical issues of recycling.
tactical_explanations:
Satisfying the present, not disempowering the future: this is the Brundtland definition in the wording of the section. The capacity is shared by the economic and environmental system. Needs and wishes apply to today and tomorrow.

Danger is to undermine future fulfillment, for example by destroying livelihoods. The statement is the line of definition, not a free description. Needs and desires are double: now and later. Dangers would mean taking the means to meet the same needs for the future system. Growth remains form, sustainability remains a condition.

The statement is true.

Much less burden is the qualitative requirement for growth, not a complete stop of every activity. The report wants a different kind, not necessary zero growth. Environmental relief is the direction. This remains possible development while the burden decreases. The statement quotes this demand clause factually.

Lower load is the qualitative requirement, not simply renaming the previous path. Sharing, long-lasting design and reprocessing are the indicated ways to get there.

The statement is true.

Today's profit maximization without looking at tomorrow is the opposite of the definition. Sustainability is the sustainability of the common system. To name only present gains, the second time pole is crossed. Future needs are the test stone. The statement fails completely.

The statement is false.

The positive goal is to satisfy people about the common system, in addition to the relief. Instead of endangering sustainability, the ability to increase. The presentation puts both into one sentence. Economy and environment remain coupled. The statement reflects this increase in system capability.

Increased system capability is the counterpart to danger. Relieving the environment and satisfying people are combined in this formulation, not as rivals.

The statement is true.

Poverty is a main topic of the report, not a blank. Recycling and reprocessing appear later as ways, not as the sole content. The limitation to technology is wrong. Our Common Future describes the extent of poverty and threats. Anyone who ignores this has not hit the section.

The statement is false.

title: European Green Deal and Taxonomy
context: Evaluate the following statements on sustainability in European economic policy:
statements: In the context of the European Green Deal, sustainability has become a key concept of European economic policy.
Sustainability reporting is mandatory for large companies from 2022 onwards.
EU taxonomy is designed to promote environmental economies, for example by improving the position of the capital market.
According to the teaching text, the European Green Deal only concerns forestry enterprises and is not considered to be the key to EU economic policy.
According to the teaching text, the reporting obligation, as from 2022, applies to all companies equally without any difference in size.
tactical_explanations:
The key concept of European economic policy is that of sustainability in the European Green Deal. It is about policy frameworks, not a voluntary fashion word. EGD is the parenthesis. Sustainability therefore migrates from the forest metaphor to the current EU governance. The statement is made about this appreciation.

The statement is true.

From 2022, large companies, mandatory: three data are provided. Reporting obligation is not a recommendation for corporations of this size. The year marks the break. Whoever shifts the obligation to an indefinite future differs from the wording. The statement remains with year, circle and character.

Compulsory, the regulation distinguishes from voluntary guidelines. The circle of the great ones is the threshold from which the report must be made, not an indefinite hope.

The statement is true.

Promoting ecological economics is the purpose of taxonomy, the better position of capital markets is the example. Capital should therefore be directed towards ecological activity. The presentation calls this channel exactly. Taxonomy is not a mere classification game here, but a support instrument about market access. The statement holds purpose and example.

Better position on the capital market means: ecologically oriented activity should facilitate financing. Taxonomy arranges activities so that capital does not flow blindly into burdensome projects.

The statement is true.

Only forestry companies would be a relapse into the word history, not the EGD statement. The Green Deal is introduced as a central economic policy for Europe. The restriction on forestry is wrong. Sustainability is a key concept of economic policy as a whole. The statement narrows down inadmissiblely.

The statement is false.

Large companies are the target group of the obligation. Without difference in size, the statement claims an all-mandatory obligation that does not formulate the representation. The qualification "large" would otherwise be superfluous. Small businesses are not equated with the same obligation as from 2022. The statement exceeds the wording.

If the presentation meant all legal forms and sizes, the word "big" was missing. The reporting obligation from 2022 is bound by this qualification and must not be stretched to the All-Rule.

The statement is false.

title: Sustainability from forestry
context: Evaluate the following statements on the origin and extension of the concept of sustainability:
statements: Originally, the term sustainability comes from forestry and described the practice of not cutting more trees than can grow back.
This basic idea should ensure a permanent wood yield and maintain the tree population.
The term sustainability is often used, but its meaning is often unclear.
Sustainability originally exclusively meant maximising short-term corporate profits.
